RFC 9110 15.5.2: 401 "indicates that the request has not been applied because it lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource." 15.5.4: 403 "the server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it... The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials. The client MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials." So "re-sending credentials will not change that" holds only for the same credentials.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `403` says the API knows who is asking and still refuses, so sending the same caller's token again changes nothing.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 15.5.2: "The server generating a 401 response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field ... containing at least one challenge". RFC 6750 s.3: "If the protected resource request included an access token and failed authentication, the resource server SHOULD include the 'error' attribute"; invalid_token: "The access token provided is expired, revoked, malformed, or invalid for other reasons." Live output matches.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, inaccurate as stated: expiry is enforced with a default clock-skew leeway, not the instant exp passes. Live, tokens signed with the real key: exp = now-60 s -> 200, now-290 s -> 200, now-310 s -> 401. Program.cs sets no ClockSkew. Same over-statement in sec 4 "once `exp` has passed, the check fails", sec 6 "a token past it is rejected", sec 8 item 4, quiz q2 option c.
issues.fix: Sec 4: "...and `exp` must not have passed (the check allows a few minutes of leeway for clock differences, so a token just past `exp` can still pass)". Sec 4 para 3: "once `exp` is more than a few minutes in the past, the check fails". Sec 6: "a token well past it is rejected". Add a claims entry (behavior, aspnetcore, source: live run exp-60 s -> 200, exp-310 s -> 401).

issues.text: Unlisted claim, wrong about ValidateIssuerSigningKey: docs say it "controls if validation of the SecurityKey that signed the securityToken is called", default false; it does not switch on the signature check (signature is checked against IssuerSigningKey regardless; wrong-key token -> 401 "The signature key was not found"). "only tokens this API issued can pass": anyone holding the key can mint one (reviewer did -> 200).
issues.quote: Each `Validate...` line switches one check on: issuer, audience, signing key, and `ValidateLifetime` for `exp`.
issues.fix: Replace the paragraph with: "`ValidateIssuer`, `ValidateAudience` and `ValidateLifetime` name the issuer, audience and `exp` checks. The signature is checked against `IssuerSigningKey`, built from the same `Jwt:SigningKey` that `JwtTokenService` signs with, so only tokens signed with that key can pass." Add both sentences to claims (source: TokenValidationParameters.ValidateIssuerSigningKey API page + live run).

issues.text: Over-strong per RFC 9110 15.5.4: the client "MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials"; logging in as a different customer can change a 403. See claim 8.
issues.quote: so logging in again changes nothing
issues.fix: Use claim 8's suggested_text: "`403` says the API knows who is asking and still refuses, so sending the same caller's token again changes nothing."

issues.text: Unlisted claim: which caller the login token identifies. True (live login as anh.tran@example.com -> payload sub "1"), but sec 2 never says which account logged in, and it is not in the ledger.
issues.quote: the request now carries a caller — customer 1, from `sub`
issues.fix: Add a claims entry (fact, source: live login anh.tran@example.com -> sub "1"), or write "the customer named in `sub`" instead of "customer 1".

issues.text: Through Caddy the header prints as `Www-Authenticate: Bearer` (live curl -i output), not `WWW-Authenticate`. A learner comparing literally may think the output differs.
issues.fix: Append to Expected result: "(curl prints the header name as `Www-Authenticate`; header names are not case-sensitive)" and add that to claims (RFC 9110 section 5.1: field names are case-insensitive).

issues.text: Key is correct, but the explanation for option b misdescribes ValidateIssuerSigningKey: it validates the signing key itself (default false); it is not the signature check that proves the API issued the token.
issues.quote: This check is about the signature and key — whether the API issued the token — not about its expiry.
issues.fix: en b: "This validates the signing key itself; it has nothing to do with `exp`." vi b: "Dòng này kiểm tra bản thân signing key; không liên quan tới `exp`."
